column1: TDE protects SQL Server data and transaction-log files {{c1::at rest}}.
column2:
The engine decrypts pages for authorized queries.
Review source

column1: SQL Server TDE encrypts database files using a symmetric {{c1::database encryption key (DEK)}}.
column2:
The DEK resides in the protected database.
Review source

column1: In certificate-based SQL Server TDE, the certificate protecting the DEK resides in {{c1::master}}.
column2:
The user database contains the protected DEK.
Review source

column1: Restoring certificate-protected TDE on another SQL Server instance requires the certificate and its {{c1::private key}}.
column2:
A database backup alone does not supply the protecting certificate and private key.
Review source

column1: Encrypt client-server traffic with {{c1::TLS}}, not TDE.
column2:
TDE protects stored data rather than the communication channel.
Review source

column1: Without secure enclaves, Always Encrypted performs column-value encryption and decryption in the {{c1::client driver}}.
column2:
The driver must support Always Encrypted and have the feature enabled.
Review source

column1: An Always Encrypted CEK is protected by a {{c1::column master key (CMK)}}.
column2:
The CMK protects the data-encryption key rather than directly encrypting column values.
Review source

column1: Always Encrypted encrypts column values with a {{c1::column encryption key (CEK)}}.
column2:
The database stores this key encrypted under a CMK.
Review source

column1: Actual Always Encrypted CMK material stays in a trusted key store {{c1::outside the database}}.
column2:
Supported choices include Azure Key Vault and Windows Certificate Store.
Review source

column1: Register metadata for an existing external CMK with {{c1::CREATE COLUMN MASTER KEY}}.
column2:
This statement does not create the external private key.
Review source

column1: The unit's Azure Key Vault-backed CMK uses KEY_STORE_PROVIDER_NAME = '{{c1::AZURE_KEY_VAULT}}'.
column2:
The corresponding client key-store provider accesses the external key.
Review source

column1: In CREATE COLUMN MASTER KEY, {{c1::KEY_PATH}} identifies the external key's location.
column2:
The database stores this location as metadata rather than storing the private key.
Review source

column1: Store metadata containing an already encrypted CEK with {{c1::CREATE COLUMN ENCRYPTION KEY}}.
column2:
Generate and encrypt the real CEK outside the database engine first.
Review source

column1: For system key-store providers, CREATE COLUMN ENCRYPTION KEY names {{c1::RSA_OAEP}} as the CEK-encryption algorithm.
column2:
This protects the CEK with the CMK rather than encrypting column data directly.
Review source

column1: Within a column's ENCRYPTED WITH clause, {{c1::COLUMN_ENCRYPTION_KEY}} selects the CEK.
column2:
The referenced key supplies encryption for the column's values.
Review source

column1: Without secure enclaves, use ENCRYPTION_TYPE = {{c1::DETERMINISTIC}} for Always Encrypted equality searches.
column2:
Encrypted operands must have compatible types, keys, and encryption settings.
Review source

column1: To hide repeated-value patterns more effectively, Always Encrypted offers ENCRYPTION_TYPE = {{c1::RANDOMIZED}}.
column2:
Without secure enclaves, this mode does not support ordinary server-side searches on those values.
Review source

column1: The unit's Always Encrypted columns use ALGORITHM = '{{c1::AEAD_AES_256_CBC_HMAC_SHA_256}}' for data encryption.
column2:
This differs from RSA_OAEP, which protects the CEK itself.
Review source

column1: Always Encrypted with secure enclaves supports computations on {{c1::plaintext}} inside isolated server memory.
column2:
This is an exception to standard Always Encrypted's client-only plaintext processing.
Review source

column1: Create a database master key with CREATE {{c1::MASTER KEY}} ENCRYPTION BY PASSWORD = '<strong-password>';
column2:
The password text is a placeholder, not a suggested password.
Review source

column1: CREATE SYMMETRIC KEY uses WITH ALGORITHM = {{c1::AES_256}} to select 256-bit AES.
column2:
The unit protects its new symmetric key with ENCRYPTION BY CERTIFICATE SensitiveDataCert.
Review source

column1: Given the unit's certificate-protected key, use {{c1::OPEN SYMMETRIC KEY}} SensitiveDataKey DECRYPTION BY CERTIFICATE SensitiveDataCert; before encryption.
column2:
Opening the key makes it available in the current session.
Review source

column1: Encrypt a value with {{c1::ENCRYPTBYKEY}}(KEY_GUID('SensitiveDataKey'), @Plaintext).
column2:
Open this certificate-protected key in the current session first.
Review source

column1: For original varchar(20) text, CONVERT(varchar(20), {{c1::DECRYPTBYKEY}}(Ciphertext)) converts decrypted bytes back to text.
column2:
Use the original data type and enough length to avoid truncation.
Review source

column1: After using the unit's open key, run {{c1::CLOSE SYMMETRIC KEY}} SensitiveDataKey; to close it.
column2:
Closing the key does not delete it or revoke permissions.
Review source

column1: SQL database in Fabric uses Azure Storage service-side encryption with {{c1::Microsoft-managed keys}} as baseline at-rest protection.
column2:
Workspace customer-managed keys enable an additional TDE layer for SQL databases.
Review source

column1: Layer TDE with {{c1::Always Encrypted}} to add sensitive-column protection against database administrators without external key access.
column2:
TDE alone does not separate authorized database access from access to plaintext values.
Review source

column1: For automatic Always Encrypted input encryption, applications pass values as client {{c1::query parameters}}, not ordinary SQL literals.
column2:
An enabled driver encrypts the parameter values before sending them to the database.
Review source

column1: Standard deterministic Always Encrypted string columns require a binary-code-point collation using {{c1::_BIN2}}.
column2:
The unit's example uses Latin1_General_BIN2.
Review source

column1: For non-NULL ciphertext, DECRYPTBYKEY returns {{c1::NULL}} when the required symmetric key is not open.
column2:
Open the correct key in the current session before decrypting.
Review source
